metadata.title: 2015 Case 19
metadata.original_presentation: A 71-year-old man with congestive heart failure and ischemic cardiomyopathy was admitted to this hospital because of sudden chest pain, diaphoresis, and shortness of breath.

required.content: What is the patient's past medical history?
required.response: The patient had hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, ischemic cardiomyopathy, and a history of myocardial infarctions.

teaching_points.content: A comprehensive medical history is crucial in understanding the patient's current condition and potential complications.

required.content: What are the patient's symptoms upon admission?
required.response: Sudden chest pain, diaphoresis, and shortness of breath.

teaching_points.content: Acute chest pain with diaphoresis and dyspnea can indicate a cardiac event and requires immediate evaluation.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary Embolism
refuting_evidence: history of ischemic cardiomyopathy and myocardial infarctions makes AMI more likely

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Aortic Dissection
refuting_evidence: absence of tearing or ripping pain description
no mention of unequal blood pressures

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Unstable Angina
refuting_evidence: sudden onset and severity of symptoms may suggest AMI instead

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Heart Failure Exacerbation
refuting_evidence: sudden chest pain and diaphoresis are more suggestive of an acute coronary syndrome

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination upon admission?
required.response: Temperature was 36.1°C, blood pressure 130/70 mm Hg, pulse 78 beats per minute and irregular, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 96%. Skin was cool, with no inflammation or hematoma over the ICD placement site.

teaching_points.content: Vital signs and physical examination findings provide essential information for assessing the patient's hemodynamic status.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI)
supporting_evidence: history of myocardial infarctions and ischemic cardiomyopathy

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary Embolism
refuting_evidence: oxygen saturation is relatively normal at 96%

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Aortic Dissection
refuting_evidence: blood pressure is not extremely high
no mention of pain radiating to the back
additional_information_needed: CT or MRI of the chest

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Arrhythmia (e.g., Atrial Fibrillation)
refuting_evidence: no direct evidence of arrhythmia causing chest pain

required.content: What were the results of the chest radiographs?
required.response: Posteroanterior and lateral chest radiographs showed a new left pleural effusion.

teaching_points.content: Chest radiographs are useful in identifying pleural effusions and other thoracic abnormalities.

required.response: Sinus rhythm with 1-mm, concave ST-segment elevations in the inferior leads and in leads V3 and V4, along with T-wave inversions and flattening in the lateral leads.

teaching_points.content: ST-segment changes on an ECG can indicate myocardial ischemia or infarction.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI)
supporting_evidence: ST-segment elevations in the inferior leads and V3, V4 on ECG

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary Embolism
refuting_evidence: ST-segment elevation not typical for PE
no evidence of right heart strain on ECG

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Congestive Heart Failure Exacerbation
refuting_evidence: ST-segment elevation not typical for CHF exacerbation

required.content: What treatments were administered upon admission?
required.response: Aspirin, magnesium sulfate, and insulin were administered. Fentanyl was given for severe pain.

teaching_points.content: Immediate management of chest pain may include analgesics and medications to address potential cardiac causes.

final_diagnosis.name: Pericarditis
key_features: Chest pain exacerbated by movement and deep inspiration
supporting_evidence: New ST-segment elevations in ECG leads
Trace pericardial effusion on cardiac ultrasonography
